business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward-integration steps and in-process recycling are described; the DRHP does not claim end-to-end integration. (1) Input-route change: "In Fiscal 2019, we transitioned from using sulphur burning furnaces to procuring liquefied sulphur dioxide (SO2) which improved production efficiency, reduced emissions and enhanced environmental compliance" – a move AWAY from in-house SO2 generation toward bought-in SO2. (2) Proposed re-integration at Manufacturing Unit – II Phase II: turnkey plant and machinery includes "a sulphur burner system, ammonium bisulphite system and Sodium metabisulphite (SMBS) system engineering and equipment"; "The use of sulphur burner technology will allow us to produce steam without relying on any external fuel sources that will significantly reduce energy costs. The waste heat boiler will generate fuel-free steam, which will be utilized across various plant operations" – energy self-generation from the process itself. (3) Locational integration: units are sited close to industries that generate liquefied SO2, securing liquid SO2, sodium carbonate, sodium hydroxide and liquid ammonia and reducing logistics cost and lead time; long-term relationships with key suppliers are stated. (4) In-process recycling: in the sodium metabisulphite route the soda ash / caustic soda slurry is mixed with "a recycled solution called mother liquor, which helps to reduce waste and reuse materials", the leftover liquid after centrifuging is recycled back into the process, and the separated crystals are dried using waste steam; in the ammonium bisulphite route "a water scrubber system is attached to trap any leftover ammonia fumes, and these captured gases are recycled back into the process to avoid waste". (5) Forward integration: none disclosed – sales are direct business-to-business to end-use customers through the Company's own sales team, with no owned distribution, warehousing or downstream processing described.

One secured working-capital facility from a financial institution is outstanding ₹125.21 lakhs against a sanctioned ₹100.00 lakhs — ₹25.21 lakhs above the limit as at 31 March 2025 (my subtraction) — inside a ₹2,100.00 lakhs sanctioned / ₹1,036.26 lakhs outstanding short-term block.

Gearing is set to rise before the project earns anything: RF 18 discloses a ₹3,400.00 lakhs HDFC term loan availed and ₹1,242.18 lakhs of placement proceeds received, which on the FY25 balance sheet would imply roughly 1.55x debt to net worth (my arithmetic), against FY25 finance cost of only ₹163.43 lakhs.

Over half the project cost is not contractually locked: purchase orders exist on 2 of 9 machinery packages (₹5,019.98 lakhs); ₹3,539.39 lakhs of machinery (41.35%) and ₹5,750.90 lakhs of the ₹10,770.88 lakhs total (53.39%) rest on quotations or the ambiguous 'Note 1' United Ventures civil line of ₹1,814.84 lakhs — all percentages my arithmetic.

The two SMBS packages worth ₹2,902.80 lakhs (33.91% of the ₹8,559.37 lakhs machinery budget, my arithmetic) sit on 30-day quotations dated 05 and 22 September 2025, expiring within roughly a month of the 26 September 2025 DRHP date, while the machinery purchase and commissioning window is January to May 2026.

Customer revenue is concentrated and uncontracted: top-1 15.10%, top-5 47.37%, top-10 68.14% of FY25 revenue; only 4 of the top ten have been customers more than five years; RF 3 states sales are governed by transactional purchase orders amendable, postponable or cancellable at the customer's discretion, and no order book is disclosed.

The single largest customer appears to be a single-country exposure: the top-1 customer amount of ₹851.21 lakhs (15.10%) is identical to the Eswatini line in the country-wise table for FY25, and the FY24 pair (₹504.50 lakhs, 11.33%) matches likewise.

verdict.our_read: Shanti Inorganics is a two-unit Gujarat maker of sulphur-based inorganic salts that earned ₹5,710.55 lakhs of revenue in FY25 (₹4,486.73 lakhs FY24, ₹4,574.21 lakhs FY23 — a 1.91% decline then a 27.28% rise, my arithmetic) at a 14.65% PAT margin and an EBITDA of ₹1,211.43 lakhs re-derived from the DRHP's own formula, with margins that have widened three years running (EBITDA margin 15.23% to 19.45% to 21.21%) as raw material fell from 54.35% to 40.76% of total income and FY25 volume rose 18.20% on a 7.04% higher realisation of ₹29.96 per kg; the profit is real but it is Vatva's profit, that unit having run at 98.03% of 18,800 MTPA while the new Bavla Unit-II, commissioned February 2025 with an equal-sized 18,000 MTPA, produced 610.00 MT — 3.39% — so ₹3,694.72 lakhs of plant and equipment bought across FY24 and FY25 (my arithmetic) currently sits behind a ₹1,223.82 lakhs revenue increase (my arithmetic), and ₹4,300.00 lakhs of Net Proceeds is sought for a further 31,200 MTPA before the last 18,000 MTPA has been shown to sell. The funding picture is tight rather than comfortable: net capital turnover is negative at (29.15) against 14.19 in FY24, a 305.43% variance the issuer attributes to higher creditors and short-term borrowings, so working capital is being carried by the payables line (the two trade-payable sub-lines rose ₹333.87 lakhs to ₹1,041.19 lakhs, my arithmetic) and by ₹1,387.25 lakhs of short-term borrowing against ₹11.26 lakhs of cash; one secured working-capital facility from a financial institution is drawn ₹125.21 lakhs against a ₹100.00 lakhs sanction, an overdrawn line as at 31 March 2025; and debt of ₹2,538.03 lakhs already about equals net worth of ₹2,586.33 lakhs (0.98x, my arithmetic), before the ₹3,400.00 lakhs HDFC term loan and ₹1,242.18 lakhs placement disclosed as already availed would take it to roughly 1.55x (my arithmetic). FY25 cash conversion looks strong — CFO ₹1,532.43 lakhs, 126.5% of EBITDA (my arithmetic) — but the three-year record is ₹2,192.05 lakhs of CFO on ₹1,797.73 lakhs of PAT (122%, my arithmetic) with FY24 at only 67.9%, and the FY25 figure leans on the same creditor stretch that turned working capital negative. Revenue security is thin at both ends: top-1/5/10 customers at 15.10%/47.37%/68.14% with only 4 of the top ten associated more than five years and no long-term contracts (RF 3 states sales run on cancellable purchase orders, and no order book is disclosed anywhere), exports at 53.83% across 14 countries and unhedged, with the largest customer's ₹851.21 lakhs identical to the Eswatini country line, and top-5/top-10 suppliers at 69.39%/96.26% with no long-term supply agreement either. Execution risk on the ₹10,770.88 lakhs Bavla project sits in paperwork not yet converted: purchase orders cover only 2 of 9 machinery packages worth ₹5,019.98 lakhs, leaving ₹3,539.39 lakhs of machinery (41.35%, my arithmetic) and ₹5,750.90 lakhs of total project cost (53.39%, my arithmetic) on quotations or an ambiguous 'Note 1' civil line, with ₹2,902.80 lakhs of SMBS packages resting on 30-day quotations dated 05 and 22 September 2025 that lapse within about a month of the 26 September 2025 filing yet fund purchases scheduled for January to May 2026, against only ₹461.64 lakhs (4.29%, my arithmetic) deployed to 31 August 2025 and no appraisal and no monitoring agency because the issue is below ₹5,000 lakhs. Governance mixes a clean litigation record — Nil for every party bar 4 direct-tax matters of ₹7.64 lakhs, contingent liabilities ₹27.70 lakhs at 1.07% of net worth, over-one-year receivables ₹22.53 lakhs at 0.87% — with a document that does not agree with itself: RF 82 says all revenue is derived from operations in India while RF 4 prints 53.83% exports; two revenue series (₹5,710.55 vs ₹5,636.83) run the full three years unreconciled; promoter holding is printed both as 83.65% and 74.85%; Vatva capacity appears as both 16,200 and 18,800 MTPA; the Group Companies paragraph names one entity while the table lists two; RF 71's body reproduces RF 69 verbatim; and FY25 EPS of ₹129.86 is struck on the pre-bonus 6,36,000 shares after a 15:1 bonus of 22 August 2025 that would put it near ₹8.12 on the 1,01,76,000 post-bonus count (my arithmetic). Capital was reshaped in the five weeks before filing — that bonus, then 13,80,200 shares placed at ₹90.00 on 17 September 2025 raising the ₹1,242.18 lakhs that appears in the project funding mix, nine days before the DRHP — while the admitted Section 203(3) breach was penalised and paid, a Section 135 CSR shortfall of ₹8.61 lakhs remains before the adjudicating officer, and challans for Form 66, Form 8, MGT-14 and PAS-3 are untraceable with the RoC application dated 26 September 2025, the DRHP's own date. With no comparable listed peer stated three times over, no market share anywhere, and the four product markets the company serves totalling USD 1,055 million globally in 2024 and growing about 3.2% a year to 2029P (my addition and my arithmetic) against 7.9% for inorganic chemicals as a category, the document offers no external anchor for its franchise claims, and the whole picture here is the DRHP as filed on 26 September 2025.

Bavla Unit-II Phase I, 18,000 MTPA installed and in commercial production from February 2025, produced 610.00 MT in FY25 — 3.39% per the Independent Chartered Engineer certificate of 20 September 2025 — while Vatva ran at 98.03% (18,429 MT of 18,800 MTPA). ₹3,694.72 lakhs of property, plant and equipment was purchased across FY24 and FY25 (my addition) against an FY25 revenue increase of ₹1,223.82 lakhs (my subtraction). Combined FY25 production of 19,039 MT (my addition) is 51.7% of the 36,800 MTPA installed after February 2025 and would be 28.0% of the 68,000 MTPA stated after Phase II (my arithmetic). Holds ISO 9001:2015, NSF, KOSHER, HACCP and HALAL, with no product recall or quality failure disclosed and no environmental proceeding outstanding. Against that, RF 19 discloses that the environmental approvals prescribe limits on aggregate production output, output of specific products and effluent discharge — the operative constraint on lifting stated capacity from 36,800 to 68,000 MTPA — Phase II approvals remain pending and are described only as routine, the Company logo and the name SHANTI are unregistered trademarks, certain approvals await a name-change application, and operations handle hazardous anhydrous ammonia and sulphur dioxide. Tax and dues exposure is small: 4 direct-tax matters of ₹7.64 lakhs, one TDS delay of ₹0.57 lakhs in FY25, contingent liabilities ₹27.70 lakhs (1.07% of net worth).

Two admitted Companies Act breaches: Section 203(3) (Avnish Manojkumar Patel as Whole-time Director and CFO while Managing Director of listed Jagjanani Textiles Limited — adjudicated, penalties paid, INC-28 filed) and Section 135 CSR of ₹8.61 lakhs for FY2023-24 neither spent nor transferred, with the Section 454 application of 22 September 2025 still pending; challans are untraceable for Form 66 (FY2011, FY2012), Form 8, MGT-14 and PAS-3, with the RoC application dated 26 September 2025, the DRHP's own date. The document contradicts itself in at least six places: RF 82 (all revenue from India) versus RF 4 (53.83% exports); two revenue series across all three years; promoter holding 83.65% versus 74.85%; Vatva capacity 16,200 versus 18,800 MTPA; the Group Companies paragraph naming one entity while the table lists two; and RF 71's body reproducing RF 69 verbatim. FY25 EPS of ₹129.86 is struck on the pre-bonus 6,36,000 count. Attrition was 57.39% in FY25; the CFO joined 25 January 2025, the Company Secretary 21 February 2025, and both Independent Directors on 04 April 2025 with no FY25 sitting fees paid.

Capital was reset in the five weeks before filing: 15:1 bonus of 95,40,000 shares on 22 August 2025, then 13,80,200 shares placed at ₹90.00 on 17 September 2025 to twelve named parties including Invicta Continuum Fund I and Amrut Bharat Opportunities Fund - Series I, raising ₹1,242.18 lakhs — 11.94% of pre-issue capital (my arithmetic) — nine days before the 26 September 2025 DRHP, and that same ₹1,242.18 lakhs is the private-placement line in the project funding mix. Non-promoter pre-issue holders lock in for one year only. On 02 December 2024 Manojkumar Jayantilal Patel transferred shares at ₹283 pre-bonus (₹17.69 post-bonus equivalent, my division) against ₹90.00 nine months later — 5.1x (my arithmetic). The 18-month weighted-average-cost-of-acquisition row and both last-5-transaction rows are printed N.A. and the accompanying narrative contradicts itself. Rameshbhai Bhimjibhai Patel holds 4.40% in the Public category despite a promoter transfer and a bonus allotment. Group Companies Bodal Chemicals Limited and Bodal Chemicals Trading Private Limited operate in a similar line with no non-compete; FY25 sales to Bodal were ₹71.68 lakhs with ₹62.74 lakhs still receivable at year end (87.53%, my arithmetic). Intermediaries: BRLM Vivro Financial Services Private Limited, Registrar KFin Technologies Limited, auditor M/s. S. N. Shah and Associates.

Net capital turnover is negative at (29.15) in FY25 against 14.19 in FY24, a 305.43% variance, on the issuer's own explanation of 'higher creditors and short-term borrowings' — working capital itself has gone negative, with trade payables at ₹1,041.19 lakhs and short-term borrowings at ₹1,387.25 lakhs against ₹11.26 lakhs of cash.

₹5,750.90 lakhs of the ₹10,770.88 lakhs project — 53.39% (my arithmetic) — is not covered by a stated purchase order; only 2 of 9 machinery packages (₹5,019.98 lakhs) are ordered, and ₹2,902.80 lakhs of SMBS engineering and equipment rests on 30-day quotations dated 05 and 22 September 2025 that lapse within roughly a month of the 26 September 2025 filing, while the purchase and commissioning window is January to May 2026.

₹4,300.00 lakhs of Net Proceeds is sought for 31,200 MTPA of new capacity while the last tranche of 18,000 MTPA at Bavla ran at 3.39% (610.00 MT) in FY25 — the DRHP seeks capital for the next plant before demonstrating offtake on the current one.

RF 82 states 'We derive all our revenue from our operations in India' while RF 4 prints ₹3,034.44 lakhs of revenue from sales outside India, 53.83% of FY25 — a direct contradiction the document never reconciles.

Two revenue series (₹5,710.55 / ₹4,486.73 / ₹4,574.21 versus ₹5,636.83 / ₹4,454.04 / ₹4,547.68 lakhs) run through the document unreconciled, and every concentration, geography and industry percentage is struck on the lower base.
Promoter holding is printed as both 83.65% (Note 13, 96,67,040 shares, Promoters and Promoter Group) and 74.85% (Note 16, 86,49,440 shares, Promoters alone) of the same pre-issue capital.

FY25 EPS of ₹129.86 corresponds to the pre-bonus 6,36,000 share count after a 15:1 bonus issue of 95,40,000 shares on 22 August 2025, five weeks before filing; no post-bonus restated EPS appears in the extraction (post-bonus equivalents about ₹8.12 and ₹7.15 — my arithmetic).

A Section 135 CSR obligation of ₹8.61 lakhs for FY2023-24 was neither spent nor transferred within the prescribed six months and the Section 454 adjudication application of 22 September 2025 was still pending at filing; a separate Section 203(3) breach was adjudicated with penalties paid.

Challans are untraceable for Form 66 (FY2011 and FY2012), Form 8 (charges filed 2011 and 2012), Form MGT-14 and Form PAS-3 (both 24 March 2015), with the remedial RoC application dated 26 September 2025 — the DRHP's own date — supported by a search report of the same date.

FY25 supplier concentration percentages imply three different purchase denominators — ₹2,458.2, ₹2,303.4 and ₹2,055.1 lakhs from the top-1, top-5 and top-10 rows (my division) — where FY24 and FY23 each reconcile to a single base.

Employee attrition of 57.39% in FY25 (from 33.73% and 22.22%) alongside a CFO in post since 25 January 2025, a Company Secretary since 21 February 2025 and both Independent Directors since 04 April 2025 — the entire compliance and oversight layer is newer than the financial period being reported.
Cash and equivalents of ₹11.26 lakhs at 31 March 2025 against ₹1,387.25 lakhs of short-term borrowings, ahead of a ₹3,400.00 lakhs term loan already availed for the project.

Top-5 suppliers at 69.39% and top-10 at 96.26% of purchases with no long-term supply agreement, against top-10 customers at 68.14% with no long-term customer contract — both sides of the chain are concentrated and uncontracted at once.

Group Companies Bodal Chemicals Limited and Bodal Chemicals Trading Private Limited are stated to be in a similar industry with main objects permitting competing lines and no non-compete agreement, and their three-year financials are not printed in the DRHP at all.
strengths_observed: Margin trajectory is up three straight years on the issuer's own printed figures: EBITDA margin 15.23% (FY23), 19.45% (FY24), 21.21% (FY25) on EBITDA of ₹696.74 / ₹872.60 / ₹1,211.43 lakhs; PAT margin 10.12% / 11.49% / 14.65% on PAT of ₹460.21 / ₹511.62 / ₹825.90 lakhs.

Input cost intensity fell materially: cost of materials consumed was 54.35%, 45.29% and 40.76% of total income in FY23, FY24 and FY25, while FY25 sales volume rose 18.20% to 18,815.00 MT and average realisation rose 7.04% to ₹29.96 per kg — volume and price moved together, not one at the other's expense.

The existing Vatva unit is fully worked: 98.03% of 18,800 MTPA in FY25 (18,429 MT produced) per the Independent Chartered Engineer certificate dated 20 September 2025, after 96.38% in FY24 and 80.46% in FY23, with product-level utilisation of 99.26% on sodium bisulphite solution/powder and 99.29% on ammonium bisulphite.

FY25 operating cash generation ran ahead of accounting profit: CFO ₹1,532.43 lakhs against EBITDA ₹1,211.43 lakhs (126.5%) and PAT ₹825.90 lakhs (185.6%) — my arithmetic — on operating profit before working-capital changes of ₹1,328.99 lakhs.
Returns remain high despite a doubling of the asset base: ROCE 27.20% and RoNW 38.00% in FY25 with net fixed assets up from ₹704.70 lakhs (FY23) to ₹4,256.47 lakhs (FY25) plus ₹524.00 lakhs of CWIP.

Litigation record is essentially clean as printed: Nil criminal, statutory/regulatory, SEBI/exchange disciplinary and material civil proceedings for the Company, Promoters, Directors, KMP/SMP and Group Companies, with the only quantified exposure 4 direct-tax matters totalling ₹7.64 lakhs (years 2018 and 2021, excluding accrued interest).

Balance-sheet hygiene items are small: contingent liabilities ₹27.70 lakhs (1.07% of net worth), a single UGVCL bank guarantee; trade receivables over one year ₹22.53 lakhs (0.87% of net worth) as at 31 March 2025.

Statutory-dues discipline is documented: Nil delays across provident fund, ESI, professional tax and labour welfare fund for all three fiscals, with a single TDS delay of ₹0.57 lakhs in FY25; total statutory dues paid ₹960.87 / ₹740.25 / ₹683.44 lakhs.

Certification stack supports regulated end-uses: ISO 9001:2015, NSF (drinking water treatment chemicals), KOSHER, HACCP and HALAL, against a customer base of 51 domestic and 21 international customers in FY25 spanning 14 export countries.
The offer is 100% fresh capital — up to 50,00,000 Equity Shares with no Offer for Sale component — so no promoter or pre-issue holder is taking money off the table in this issue.

The Phase II land is already owned and paid for from internal accruals: Plot 6 (₹150.00 lakhs, agreement 11 July 2023) and Plot 7 (₹86.16 lakhs, agreement 16 November 2024), about 17,212.07 sq.mt. in total, and the DRHP states no portion of Net Proceeds goes to land.

Real money is already committed to the two largest machinery packages: purchase orders SICPL/PO/00102/25-26 (₹2,784.87 lakhs, Harickson Solutions LLP) and SICPL/PO/00101/25-26 (₹2,235.11 lakhs, A.H. Lundberg Systems and Haricksons, Canada), both dated 25 April 2025, with advances of ₹453.02 lakhs already paid across six instalments (my addition), and ₹461.64 lakhs of the project deployed from internal accruals to 31 August 2025.

Procurement conditions are stated conservatively: no second-hand or used machinery out of the Net Proceeds, and the DRHP states Promoters, Directors and KMP have no interest in the civil works, plant and machinery, utilities or the quoting vendors.

Process design targets energy self-supply: the Phase II sulphur burner with waste heat boiler is stated to generate fuel-free steam for plant operations, alongside existing mother-liquor recycling in the SMBS route and an ammonia scrubber recycling captured gases in the ABS route.

Related-party quantum is small relative to scale: the largest single item is ₹71.68 lakhs of FY25 sales to Bodal Chemicals Limited (1.27% of the ₹5,636.83 lakhs revenue series, my arithmetic), and promoter remuneration is ₹36.00 lakhs each for FY25.
